f_ir.name: loss_kl_divergence_001_advantage_stabilized
f_ir.intuition: Simplified and stabilized the KL divergence computation by clamping the probabilities to avoid log(0) and numerical instability. Replaced mean aggregation to better stabilize gradient scale with weighted mean respecting sample weights. Ensured weights default safely to ones if missing. This reduces numerical stress and avoids instability with very small or large values in target and predicted probabilities.
f_ir.pseudocode:
p = sigmoid(log_prob_w - log_prob_l)
target = sigmoid(advantage_w - advantage_l)
p = clamp(p, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
target = clamp(target, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
loss = target * log(target / p) + (1 - target) * log((1 - target) / (1 - p))
weighted_loss = loss * weight
final_loss = mean(weighted_loss)
f_ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    advantage_w = batch['advantage_w']
    advantage_l = batch['advantage_l']
    weight = batch.get('weight', ops.ones_like(lpw))
    
    p = ops.sigmoid(ops.sub(lpw, lpl))
    target = ops.sigmoid(ops.sub(advantage_w, advantage_l))
    
    epsilon = 1e-6
    p = ops.clamp(p, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
    target = ops.clamp(target, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
    
    term1 = ops.mul(target, ops.log(ops.div(target, p)))
    term2 = ops.mul(ops.sub(ops.ones_like(target), target),
                     ops.log(ops.div(ops.sub(ops.ones_like(target), target), ops.sub(ops.ones_like(p), p))))
    kl = ops.add(term1, term2)
    weighted_kl = ops.mul(kl, weight)
    return ops.mean(weighted_kl)
